data.narrative:
Phasecraft is a Series A quantum computing company founded by Montanaro, Cubitt, and Morton, having raised $25M to date. The quantum computing sector contains 11 identifiable peers: 3 publicly traded firms (IonQ, Rigetti Computing, D-Wave Quantum) and 8 private companies including Quantinuum and Infleqtion.

Valuation triangulation relied on a single applicable method due to peer constraints. The Stage-Progression approach applies a 2.0x multiplier to the $25M raised proxy, reflecting typical step-ups from Series A to subsequent rounds, yielding an implied valuation of $50M. Peer-Median analysis was not applicable; while 5 same-sector peers exist, none met the narrow filters required (same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar valuation tier) to provide three or more comparable datapoints. A broad all-sector median would introduce unacceptable noise given the specialized nature of quantum computing valuations.

The analysis supports a median valuation of $50M, with a reasonable range of $42M to $57M reflecting methodological bounds around the stage-progression estimate. Key uncertainties stem from the limited peer set—the quantum computing sector remains early-stage and heterogeneous in business model and technical approach—and the absence of direct same-stage comparables. Any valuation outside this range would require material new information on Phasecraft's technical milestones, IP position, or customer commitments.
